submission.natural_language_explanation: A topic dial for English prose about people and their lives (news, biography, entertainment, family, personal anecdote). Inside such prose it fires on the word that opens or links the next noun phrase: 'a'/'the', numerals ('two', 'three'), quantifiers ('several'), 'by' after 'written'/'followed', 'to' after 'married', 'and' between two people's names. It also fires on person-role words ('former', 'president', 'spokesman', 'wife', 'daughter', 'debut', 'born'). The same function words in code, software or technical documentation, legal clauses and engineering or product descriptions stay well below the active line (about 0.3-0.6 of 3.1). The quantifiers 'a few' and 'a couple' fire in any prose. General non-human descriptive prose (weather, geography, markets) is only weakly to moderately active, and math text is uneven and not claimed.

rival_explanations: Broader: a general natural-prose detector. It fires on determiners, numerals and prepositions in any discursive English, whether it is about people, nature or markets, and is suppressed only in code and markup. This predicts equally strong firing on weather, geography or finance prose.

Narrower: a token-gated quantity and noun-phrase-onset detector. It fires on 'a few', 'a couple', 'several', small numerals and 'a'/'the' at the start of a noun phrase, whatever the topic. This predicts that technical sentences such as 'runs in two pods' or 'followed by a reboot' fire as strongly as biographical ones.
